title: New comprehensive zoning bylaw approved
subtitle: Also: rooftop sign variance approved, sustainable development checklist, Delhi Street heritage designation, driveway and parking rules, winter parking review.
overview: Council approved Guelph's first comprehensive zoning bylaw in 28 years, along with a companion Official Plan Amendment, after amending it in several places {{vote:m19}}. The bylaw replaces the 1995 rules and permits more housing types across residential areas.

Council made changes that affect everyday life on residential streets. It relaxed driveway width limits for semi-detached homes and on-street townhouses {{vote:m11}}, allowed wider driveways and garages for single detached homes on narrower lots, kept current apartment parking minimums outside the downtown {{vote:m9}}, and removed the 80 square metre size cap on additional residential units {{vote:m18}}. Staff will also report back on allowing more than three units per lot, now due by the end of Q1 2025 {{vote:m16}}.

Council also approved the Sustainable Development Checklist for site plan applications {{vote:m5}}, agreed to publish notice of intent to designate 65 Delhi Street under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m1}}, and approved two SV Law fascia signs at 245 Hanlon Creek Boulevard {{vote:m4}}. Staff will look at removing winter on-street parking restrictions {{vote:m20}}.

decisions.item: Comprehensive Zoning Bylaw and Official Plan Amendment 88
decisions.detail: Council approved the new Comprehensive Zoning Bylaw and companion Official Plan Amendment as amended, which includes a staff report on units beyond three per lot {{vote:m19}}.
Council changed the maximum driveway width table, relaxing limits for semi-detached homes and on-street townhouses {{vote:m11}}.
Council set apartment parking at 1.5 spaces per unit for the first 20 units and 1.25 after that, with 20% for visitors, outside the downtown, keeping the current requirements {{vote:m9}}.
Council directed staff to remove the 80 square metre maximum size for additional residential units {{vote:m18}}.

decisions.item: More than three units per lot
decisions.detail: Council directed staff to consider as-of-right permissions for more than three units in low density areas and report back by the end of Q1 2025 {{vote:m16}}.

decisions.item: SV Law signs at 245 Hanlon Creek Boulevard
decisions.detail: Council approved two fascia signs on the third storey, overriding the staff recommendation to refuse, and rejected a proposal to require them to be non-illuminated {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the checklist for use by staff in the site plan approval process {{vote:m5}}.
Council directed staff to investigate removing winter on-street parking restrictions through the city-wide parking review {{vote:m20}}.

debate: On the Hanlon Creek Boulevard signs, a delegate for the law firm said the signs met the bylaw's variance criteria, matched neighbouring illuminated signs, and drew no opposition. Staff said the 2021 sign bylaw removed top-storey illumination to cut light pollution and support climate targets.

A councillor pushed for non-illuminated signs, citing migratory birds and light pollution. Others said the signs matched their neighbours, and the non-illuminated amendment failed {{vote:m3}}. A broader light trespass review is planned.

On driveways, supporters of wider limits described residents facing court fines for parking on decorative walkways and called it an affordability issue. Opponents and staff said less green space threatens stormwater management and tree survival.

On garage projections, staff and several councillors argued that garages ahead of the front wall reduce eyes on the street and harm street character. The proposal to allow a two-metre projection was defeated {{vote:m10}}.

On parking and basement units, supporters of higher apartment parking cited overflow on-street parking and bylaw calls. A proposal to limit basement units to two bedrooms was defeated {{vote:m13}} after councillors cited families needing larger units.
